proposal.title: Private S3 test bucket with scoped existing-operator access
proposal.body: Scope: one proposed private Amazon S3 bucket (Block Public Access, server-side encryption, versioning) for synthetic text documents, plus the existing IAM operator as an external caller with one s3-read-write access contract. No AI, database or web app. Assumptions: region not yet selected; operator ARN supplied later as a Terraform input; identity not verified; delete permission must be confirmed against the s3-read-write contract. No deployment.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Stops accidental public exposure and allows recovery of overwritten objects.
requirementDrafts.basis: "Keep public access blocked and enable encryption and versioning."
requirementDrafts.statement: Proposed: the test bucket blocks all public access and enables server-side encryption and object versioning.

requirementDrafts.rationale: An explicit least-privilege contract avoids broad grants. Unconfirmed delete permission could cause failures during test cleanup.
requirementDrafts.basis: "An existing IAM operator needs upload, read and delete access."
requirementDrafts.statement: Proposed: only the existing IAM operator can upload, read and delete objects. No other principal gets access, and delete coverage must be confirmed in the typed contract.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Clear limits keep the deployment test small and reviewable.

response.message: Good news: the local emulation of design revision 2 passed with no failures, blockers or gaps, so the bucket and the operator's storage calls behave as expected against the emulated S3 API. That is not proof of real IAM enforcement, and delete permission is still an open item because the typed read/write access may not cover deletes, so we won't change the diagram yet. Which country should the test documents stay in, so we can record that and then pick an AWS region for a real Terraform plan check?
